title: Meat Pizza, Whole Wheat Thick Crust

content.title: About
content.content: Meat pizza on a whole wheat thick crust combines a savory tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, a variety of meat toppings (ham, sausage, beef) and a crunchy, nutrient‑rich crust made from whole‑grain flour. This pizza offers a rich meat flavor together with the benefits of whole grains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole wheat crust provides more fiber and micronutrients than a standard white crust.
Tomatoes used in the sauce are high in lycopene, an antioxidant that supports heart health.
Meat toppings often include lean beef pieces, boosting the protein content.
Pizza originated in Naples, but today its variations are adapted to local tastes worldwide.
A thick crust retains more moisture, making each bite juicier.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Meat and cheese supply high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Fiber from whole grains
items.content: Whole wheat flour increases dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and whole grains contain B1, B3, B6 vitamins that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, helping protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Mozzarella provides calcium and phosphorus important for bones and teeth.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The thick crust and cheese make the pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Processed meat toppings can contain saturated fats that may affect cholesterol levels if consumed excessively.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salty meats and cheese increase sodium intake.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole wheat flour contains gluten, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Potential additives
items.content: Some pre‑made meat toppings may contain preservatives; choose fresh ingredients when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pizza into serving pieces and enjoy it hot. Adding fresh vegetables such as arugula or cherry tomatoes after baking enhances flavor and adds vitamins.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to keep the crust crisp.
